Question: How do changes progress through environments
Value: 1: We deploy manually to all environments

Value: 3: All checks happen as part of the deployment pipeline

Question: Build artifacts
Value: 1: The build step creates a new package each time the software is promoted to the next environment
Value: 3: The package is built once and the same package is used each time the software is promoted to the next environment

Question: Deployment process
Value: 1: The deployment process might be updated between environments, for example if we find a step was missing or a config value had changed
Value: 3: The deployment process is versioned alongside the package to keep it the same on all environments, changes would mean starting from the first environment again

Question: After you deploy to an environment
Value: 1: We depend on testers to check it's working
Value: 3: An automated test or script checks the application is running and its dependencies are available

Question: Environment similarity
Value: 1: Our pre-production environments have significant differences to the production environment
Value: 2: Our pre-production environments are mostly the same as production, with non-critical differences, like not needing the application firewall or load-balancers we use in production
Value: 3: Our pre-productions are very similar to the production environment

Question: Infrastructure changes
Value: 1: All changes are manual and we're not certain environments are kept in sync when changes are made
Value: 2: All changes are manual but we progress changes through our environments like we do code changes to keep them in sync and test our changes

Question: New features
Value: 1: New features appear when we deploy

Question: New features
Value: 1: All users get a new feature at the same time
